# Power station and solar combos for an RV

I only have one direct purchase link (the ALLPOWERS). For the others I've linked the review pages I used, so check current prices at the retailer.

## Size it first
- A fridge at ~150 W for 10 hours is about 1,500 Wh. [Acquired Sense](https://www.acquiredsense.com/reviews/power-stations.html)
- A 13,500 BTU roof AC draws ~1,500 W running and spikes past 3,000 W at startup. To run it, you need a unit with at least 3,000 W of output. [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)
- Check the unit's maximum solar input. A big roof array is wasted if the station caps below it. [GetWattLogic](https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life)

## My picks

**Best for an RV with AC or full-time boondocking: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3**
- It has 4,096 Wh, 4,000 W continuous and 8,000 W surge, expandable past 12 kWh.
- It recharges 0-80% in about 50 minutes from a wall outlet.
- It's heavy, a two-person lift, and the most expensive option once you add batteries. [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)
- The older DELTA Pro (3,600 Wh, 30A RV outlet, 1,600 W solar input) was listed at $2,199. [Outdoor Power Stations](https://outdoorpowerstations.com/articles/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti)

**Best value for big capacity: ALLPOWERS R4000**
- It has 3,456 Wh LiFePO4, 3,600 W at 120 V (6,000 W peak), and a dedicated RV outlet.
- Solar input is up to 2,000 W across three inputs of 650 W each. You need panels on all three to reach 2,000 W.
- It weighs 45 kg (~99 lb), so it's more of a fixed install than a portable unit.
- It has a 5-year warranty. Returns are 30 days, and sale items can't be returned.
- The store price is $1,499. Code EXTRA12 (12% off orders over $1,200, expires 2026-11-15) was tested at $1,319.12. Stores usually take one code per order, and checkout has the final word.
- [Buy at ALLPOWERS](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh) (affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you). [Details](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh)

**Mid-range with a 30A RV port: BLUETTI AC200L**
- It has 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W output, a built-in 30A RV outlet, and up to 1,200 W solar input.
- It weighs ~62 lb. [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/), [Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)
- Don't confuse it with the older AC200P, which is limited to 700 W of solar and recharges slowly. [Outdoor Power Stations](https://outdoorpowerstations.com/articles/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti)

**Lighter weekend setup (no roof AC): Jackery Explorer 1000 Plus or EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus**
- The Jackery 1000 Plus has 1,264 Wh and weighs ~14.5 kg. It's enough for a fridge, Starlink Mini and laptop overnight. [NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife)
- The DELTA 3 Plus has 1,024 Wh, 1,800 W and accepts up to 1,000 W of solar. The Jackery 1000 v2 tops out at 400 W. [Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)

## Solar panels
- For portable folding panels, 300-400 W refills a mid-size unit in a full day of decent sun. [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)
- The Renogy 200W Foldable Solar Suitcase is one suggested pairing for 1-2 kWh units. [NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife)
- Keep panel voltage and current within the station's input limits. Bundle wattage varies by package, so check what's included.
- If you want the max solar speed on a big unit, EcoFlow and Bluetti flagships accept the most. [Acquired Sense](https://www.acquiredsense.com/reviews/power-stations.html)

## Caveats
- The EmergencyEnergy guide is written for Ontario, Canada. The capacity and output comparisons apply, but its electrical code references don't. Hardwiring to an RV inlet should still go through a qualified electrician.
- Several of these sources are affiliate sites, and prices change often.

Tell me whether you run roof AC and how many nights you boondock, and I can narrow this to one pick and a panel count.
